Hi Priyom,

I signed up for Redwood via the self-serve flow yesterday (thanks — looks promising). We're evaluating how Redwood would fit into our OSS contributor workflow — specifically the GitHub integration and webhooks. A few quick questions up front:

- Do you support a GitHub App install (recommended) vs OAuth token? We prefer the App for org-level permissions.
- What webhook scopes/events do you need to ingest PR/issue activity? Any special requirements for private repos?
- Can you do a quick run-through of how the KV cache/prefix caching would behave for a repo-driven prompt set?

Would love a 30–45 minute demo + technical Q&A with an SE on the call. Our core folks who should join: me (product), Samir (backend), and maybe our infra lead if needed. We're on US Eastern (EDT).

Proposed windows: Mon 4/26 afternoon EDT (13:00–17:00) or Tue 4/27 morning EDT. Any availability?

I attached a screenshot of our current webhook settings (screenshot-webhook-perms.png) to show what we have today.

Thanks — Ava

Hi Ava — great to meet you and welcome aboard!

Short answers up front: we strongly prefer a GitHub App install for org-level installs (it's more reliable for webhooks and token rotation). For webhooks we consume Issues, Pull Request events (opened/edited/closed), and Push events for repo activity; for private repos an App with Repo scope is required — we do not request admin permissions unless you opt into auto-install. KV/prefix caching depends mostly on prompt access patterns; we'll discuss concrete tuning during the call.

Ben (SE) is CC'd — he can dive into the architecture and permissions on the demo.

I have the following slots open (all EDT converted below):
- Mon 4/26 14:00–14:45 EDT (45m)
- Mon 4/26 16:00–16:30 EDT (30m)
- Tue 4/27 10:00–10:45 EDT (45m)

If any of these work, I can send a calendar invite (we use Google Meet). Alternatively, here is my Calendly if you prefer to pick: https://calendly.com/priyom/redwood-demo

Draft agenda I propose:
1) 10–15m product demo (integration flow + repo onboarding)
2) 15–20m SE deep-dive (webhook scopes, auth patterns, KV/cache behavior)
3) 5–10m next steps/rollout plan

If you can share whether you'll need detailed security/compliance notes (SOC2 artifacts) beforehand, I can attach them.

Thanks — looking forward to it.

— Priyom Das
SDR (Inbound) | Redwood Inference
